cards.stem: In a survey, 60 senior cycle students and 80 junior cycle students were asked which sport they would prefer to have in their school: tag rugby or pickleball.
cards.questionText: (i) Find the total number of students in the survey. (ii) 70% of the 60 senior cycle students chose tag rugby. Find the number of senior cycle students who chose tag rugby.

cards.stem: In a survey, 60 senior cycle students and 80 junior cycle students were asked which sport they would prefer to have in their school: tag rugby or pickleball.
cards.questionText: 3/5 of the 80 junior cycle students chose pickleball. Find the number of junior cycle students who did not choose pickleball.

cards.stem: Patrick had to do the following calculation: (7·35 + 2·53)/4·6.
cards.questionText: (i) First, he made an estimate of what the answer should be. To do this, he wrote each number correct to the nearest whole number. Fill in the boxes below to find Patrick’s estimate. (ii) Patrick then used his calculator and got 7·9 as his answer. He knows from his estimate that this is incorrect. Patrick keyed the following buttons into his calculator: 7·35 + 2·53 ÷ 4·6 =. What should Patrick key into his calculator to get the correct answer?

cards.stem: Olivia is buying strawberries and cream. Olivia buys 6 punnets of strawberries. The number of strawberries in each punnet is given below: 14, 15, 16, 15, 11, 13.
cards.questionText: (i) Find the mode of the data. (ii) Find the mean of the data.

cards.stem: A 200 ml container of cream costs €2·49. The cream is on special offer, where you get 3 containers for the price of 2.
cards.questionText: Find the total cost of 1200 ml of cream, using this special offer.

cards.stem: The supermarket sells punnets of strawberries in two sizes, large and small. Large punnet: 500 grams, €5·50. Small punnet: 300 grams, €2·95.
cards.questionText: Which punnet works out better value for money, the large punnet or the small punnet? Use calculations to support your answer. Tick one box only.

cards.stem: A group of students carry out an experiment to see how exercise affects their heart rates. 10 students measure their heart rates before exercise. The results are shown in the stem and leaf diagram below.
cards.questionText: (i) Find the median of the data. (ii) Find the range of the data.

cards.stem: A group of students carry out an experiment to see how exercise affects their heart rates. 10 students measure their heart rates before exercise. The results are shown in the stem and leaf diagram below.
cards.questionText: The same 10 students measure their heart rates again after exercise. The median heart rate after exercise is 102. The range of the heart rates after exercise is 24. Describe how exercise affects the students’ heart rates. Use the information from both the median and the range in your answer.
solutionQuotes: The hearts rates have increased but the spread is the same.

cards.stem: Ben rolls a fair, six-sided die numbered 1 to 6. The three events A, B, and C are listed below: A: Ben rolls an even number. B: Ben rolls a number less than 7. C: Ben rolls a 3.
cards.questionText: (i) Write each of the letters A, B, and C into the correct box on the probability scale below, to show the probability of each event. (ii) Another event, D, is marked on the probability scale above. Give an example of an event that has the same probability as event D.

cards.questionText: Draw pattern 4 of the sequence.
solutionQuotes: Some work of merit, for example one or more extra box added to pattern 3

cards.questionText: (b) Complete the table below to show the number of squares in each of the first six patterns. (c) What type of sequence is made by the number of squares in each pattern? Give a reason for your answer. Type of sequence: Linear or Non-linear. Tick one box only.

cards.stem: The number of squares in pattern n of the sequence can be found using the formula: Number of squares = 4n − 3.
cards.questionText: (i) How many squares are in pattern 63 of the sequence? (ii) Pattern k has exactly 373 squares. Find the value of k.

cards.stem: Norma walked from her home to the shop. The distance-time graph below shows her distance from home, along the route travelled, for her walk. Three stages of the graph are labelled A, B, and C. Use the graph to answer parts (a), (b), and (c).
cards.questionText: (a) During stage B, Norma stopped to check her phone. (i) How far had Norma walked when she stopped to check her phone? Give your answer in metres. (ii) For how many seconds was Norma stopped during stage B? (b) In which of the two stages, A or C, did Norma walk the fastest? Give a reason for your answer, based on the graph. Tick one box only.

cards.questionText: Continue the graph on the previous page to show this information.

cards.questionText: Find Norma’s average speed, in metres/second, on her walk home. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

cards.stem: Barry charges his phone for 90 minutes. The graph below shows the battery charge on his phone from when the charging starts (t = 0) until it is unplugged (t = 90). A battery charge of 100 means that the battery is fully charged.
cards.questionText: Use the graph to answer parts (a)(i) and (a)(ii): (i) Complete the following sentence: “Barry’s phone has a battery charge of [blank] when the charging starts, and it increases by [blank] every 10 minutes.” (ii) The slope of the graph changes at 50 minutes. Explain why this happens in the context of the question.

A battery charge of 100 means that the battery is fully charged. Alice has a battery charge of 85 on her phone when Barry starts charging his phone. Alice watches a film on her phone for the 90 minutes and her battery charge decreases by 5 every 10 minutes.
cards.questionText: (i) Complete the table below to show the battery charge on Alice’s phone every 10 minutes for the first 60 minutes. (ii) Use the values from the table above to draw a graph of the battery charge on Alice’s phone on the diagram on the previous page, from t = 0 to t = 90, for t ∈ ℝ.

cards.questionText: The numbers in the table in part (b)(i) follow a pattern where C is the battery charge on Alice’s phone, and t is the time in minutes since the charging started. Which one of the following formulae shows the pattern in the table? Justify your answer. C = 85 + 0·5t; C = 0·5 − 85t; C = 85 − 0·5t. Tick one box only.

cards.questionText: (a) Complete the table above by filling in the missing value. Remember that there are 30 students in total. (b) Complete the histogram below to show the information in the table. One bar has been done for you.

cards.questionText: (c) What is the greatest number of students who could spend less than 15 minutes on average doing maths homework? (d) Find the percentage of students who spend 40 minutes or more on average doing maths homework. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

cards.questionText: (i) The length of the side [AD] is 5 cm. Find the length of the side [PS]. (ii) The area of the smaller quadrilateral ABCD is 42 cm². Find the area, in cm², of the bigger quadrilateral PQRS.

cards.stem: Sima makes a skateboard ramp. The ramp is in the shape of a right-angled triangle. A diagram of the ramp is shown below. The lengths of two sides of the triangle are shown. The angle A is marked.
cards.questionText: (i) Fill in the table below to show the length of the side opposite the angle A and the length of the side adjacent to the angle A. (ii) Use the lengths from part (b)(i) to write down the value of tan A as a fraction. (iii) Hence, find the size of the angle A. Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

cards.stem: Debbie owns a bus hire company. Debbie wants to buy a new bus. She must choose a bus size, an engine type, and a colour from the table below. Bus size: Minibus, Coach, Double-decker. Engine type: Electric, Diesel. Colour: White, Blue, Green, Red.
cards.questionText: (i) Find how many different choices of bus are possible. For example, one possible choice is minibus, electric engine and white. (ii) Debbie does not want a bus that is double-decker or has an electric engine. How many different choices of bus are now possible?

cards.stem: Debbie buys 370 litres of diesel. The cost of diesel excluding VAT is €1·75 per litre. VAT is charged at 13·5%.
cards.questionText: Work out the total cost of Debbie’s diesel including VAT. Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.

cards.stem: The fuel tank of the diesel engine is in the shape of a rectangular solid that is 100 cm long, 75 cm wide and 65 cm high, as shown in the diagram below.
cards.questionText: Find the volume of the fuel tank in litres. Note: 1 litre = 1000 cm³.

cards.stem: Debbie brings a school group from Sligo to Galway. Debbie leaves Sligo at 08:45. The journey takes 2 hours and 38 minutes.
cards.questionText: What time does she arrive in Galway?

cards.stem: There are 54 passengers on the bus, made up of teachers and students. The ratio of teachers to students is 1:8.
cards.questionText: Work out how many students are on the bus.

cards.stem: The oil tank of a bus is shown below. It has a large cylindrical section on the bottom with a narrower cylindrical section on top. Oil is poured into the empty tank at a steady rate until it is full.
cards.questionText: Which of the graphs above shows the height of the oil in the tank after time (t)? Give a reason for your answer. Tick one box only: Graph A, Graph B, Graph C.

cards.stem: Anthony works in a shop. His basic rate of pay is €15·80 per hour, for the first 35 hours he works in a week.
cards.questionText: (i) Find Anthony’s gross pay for a week if he works 35 hours. (ii) Anthony gets paid 50% extra for each overtime hour, that is, for every extra hour he works over the 35 hours. Find the amount Anthony gets paid for 1 overtime hour.

cards.stem: Anthony works in a shop. His basic rate of pay is €15·80 per hour, for the first 35 hours he works in a week. Anthony gets paid 50% extra for each overtime hour, that is, for every extra hour he works over the 35 hours.
cards.questionText: Anthony’s gross pay for last week was €671·50. Using your answers from parts (a)(i) and (a)(ii), find how many overtime hours Anthony worked last week.

cards.stem: In 2025, Anthony’s gross income was €35 000.
cards.questionText: (i) He paid income tax at a rate of 20%. Find Anthony’s gross tax for the year. (ii) Anthony had an annual tax credit of €4000. Find Anthony’s net tax for the year.

cards.questionText: Anthony also paid a total of €1445 in PRSI and a total of €596 in USC. Find Anthony’s net annual income after deductions of income tax, PRSI, and USC.

cards.stem: Anthony saves €50 per week.
cards.questionText: How much does he save in one year? (You may assume there are 52 weeks in a year.)

cards.stem: Anthony puts €2000 in a savings account. The interest rate is 3% compound interest per year. At the end of the first year Anthony puts another €1000 into the account.
cards.questionText: Find how much is in Anthony’s savings account after 2 years?
